AVX batched SHA-256 hashing with tail padding and result stores

# Purpose
[`fd_sha256_private_batch_avx`](<#fd_sha256_private_batch_avx>) implements a batched SHA-256 hash routine that uses AVX vector types and lane-based processing to hash up to `FD_SHA256_BATCH_MAX` messages in one call. The function first checks the batch size and falls back to the scalar `fd_sha256_hash` function when the batch is too small. For larger batches, it builds the SHA-256 tail blocks for each message in scratch memory, adds the SHA padding and message length, and then processes the message blocks in parallel across vector lanes.

The main loop loads 8 message streams, transposes the input words into vector form, and runs the 64 SHA-256 rounds with the standard `Sigma`, `sigma`, `Ch`, and `Maj` operations and the `fd_sha256_K` constants. It tracks which lanes still have data, switches lanes to the padded tail blocks when needed, and updates the hash state only for active lanes. At the end, it transposes the state back and stores the final digests to the output buffers. This file is an internal implementation file for the SHA-256 batch path, not a public API header.
